meta.not_here: The DCF side is curated by hand. An empty dcf_item means NOT YET CHECKED, never that the question was not asked.

sections.name: School Profile

sections.summary: Buildings, rooms, toilets, water, electricity, library, playground and computers. A yes/no here is often a type code with eight values.

examples.label: A yes/no that is eight codes
examples.wrong: 50.0% of government schools fail the RTE boundary-wall norm
examples.why: boundary_wall = 1 means Pucca. Code 5 is the only 'no wall'. Codes 2, 3, 4 and 7 are broken walls, fencing, hedges and partial walls. RTE Schedule item (vii) accepts a boundary wall OR fencing.

examples.label: A join that returns nothing, silently
examples.why: UDISE spells the school key psuedocode before 2022-23 and pseudocode after. A unioned table holds both columns. Each is null in the other era. A join on one name drops half the series and raises nothing.

examples.label: Two columns that contradict each other
examples.right: 5,845 of them report no library at all
examples.why: DCF 2.11(b) asks about a librarian. No gate sits above 2.11(a). 4,633 of these schools report no library, no book bank and no reading corner. In Bihar the contradiction reaches 19.1% of all librarian claims.

recipes.title: Build a school panel that survives the 2022-23 break
recipes.problem: You want the same school across eight releases. A join on the obvious key returns nothing for half the series. It raises no error.
recipes.sql:
-- The key is spelled two ways and each is null in the other era.
-- Coalesce BOTH sides or you silently lose 2018-19 to 2021-22.
with k as (
  select coalesce(pseudocode, psuedocode) as school_id, year, *
  from raw_profile_data_1
)
select school_id, count(distinct year) as years_present
from k group by 1 having count(distinct year) = 8;
recipes.result: 1,370,329 schools appear in all eight releases. The key is stable. Across the 1,414,172 present in both 2022-23 and 2025-26, the state matches 100.00%.

recipes.title: Measure the government-to-private shift
recipes.problem: Sector is not a column. You derive it from a management code. The current form omits two of those codes. 21,330 schools still report them.
recipes.sql:
-- Map EVERY code present in the data, including 8 and 98 which the
-- 2025-26 form no longer prints. Omitting them renders 21,330 schools NULL.
select year,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when sector='govt'    then enrol else 0 end) / sum(enrol), 2) as govt_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when sector='private' then enrol else 0 end) / sum(enrol), 2) as private_pct
from school_year join school_enrol using (school_id, year)
where year in ('2022-23','2025-26') group by 1;
recipes.result: Government moves 55.37% to 49.66%. Private moves 32.93% to 38.64%. The two shift by exactly 5.71 points in opposite directions. Government falls below half.

recipes.title: Count schools with no library, honestly
recipes.problem: Three columns answer one question. States answer it under different conventions. A fourth column contradicts them in 5,845 schools.
recipes.sql:
-- Compare a state's three rows against EACH OTHER before comparing states.
select y.state,
  round(avg(case when l.library_availability=1 then 100.0 else 0 end),1) as library,
  round(avg(case when l.book_bank=1            then 100.0 else 0 end),1) as book_bank,
  round(avg(case when l.reading_corner=1       then 100.0 else 0 end),1) as reading_corner,
  sum(case when l.librarian_yn=1 and l.library_availability=2 then 1 else 0 end) as contradictions
from school_library l join school_year y using (school_id, year)
where l.year='2025-26' and y.sector='govt' group by 1 order by 2;
recipes.result: Karnataka government reports 98.5 / 89.6 / 87.7. Rajasthan government reports 77.8 / 17.6 / 27.9. A 72-point gap on book banks is a reporting convention. It is not a difference in books.

recipes.title: Follow an age cohort instead of a grade
recipes.problem: Grade-to-grade transition confuses repetition with exit. Age does not. A child who repeats a class still ages one year.
recipes.sql:
-- item_group 8 in raw_enrolment_data_2 is AGE; item_id is the age in years.
-- The values live in c<N>_b and c<N>_g. c<N>_t exists and is empty: it sums to 35
-- across a million rows, so summing it returns a plausible, wrong, tiny number.
select e.year, e.item_id::int as age,
       sum(coalesce(c1_b,0)+coalesce(c1_g,0) /* ...c2..c12 */) as pupils
from raw_enrolment_data_2 e
where e.item_group='8' and e.year in ('2022-23','2025-26')
group by 1,2 order by 2;
recipes.result: Age 12 in 2022-23, measured at age 15 in 2025-26. Bihar 60.7%. Gujarat 63.4%. Kerala 97.1%. Read the caveat. Since 2022-23 a student progresses by default. This counts registry state, not attendance.

traps.what: A column that looks like a yes/no is a TYPE code. Read `= 1` as the affirmative and every other type becomes a negative.
traps.cost: We read boundary_wall = 1 as 'has a wall'. We reported that 50.0% of government schools fail the RTE norm. Only code 5 means no wall. The correct figure is 25.1%.
traps.check: Compare the count of distinct values in the data against the count of codes in that year's DCF.
traps.fix:
-- WRONG: counts every non-pucca barrier as a failure
avg(case when boundary_wall = 1 then 100.0 else 0 end)

-- RIGHT: code 5 is the only 'no wall'; 1,2,3,4,7 all secure the building
avg(case when boundary_wall = 5 then 100.0 else 0 end)  -- share with NO wall
avg(case when boundary_wall in (1,2,3,4,7) then 100.0 else 0 end)  -- share secured

traps.what: UDISE spells the school key `psuedocode` before 2022-23. It spells it `pseudocode` after. A unioned table holds both columns. Each column is null in the other era.
traps.cost: A join on one name returns ZERO rows for half the series. It raises no error. The pair drops out. The field then looks younger than it is.
traps.check: Coalesce both spellings on BOTH sides of any join.
traps.fix:
-- WRONG: returns ZERO rows for 2018-19..2021-22, silently
join b on b.pseudocode = a.pseudocode

-- RIGHT: both sides, every year
join b on coalesce(b.pseudocode, b.psuedocode)
        = coalesce(a.pseudocode, a.psuedocode)

traps.what: `urinla_girls` is a transposition. It is corrected to `urinal_girls` at 2022-23.
traps.cost: A name-based series breaks at the break year.

traps.what: The source spells panchayat as `panchyat` up to 2020-21.
traps.cost: A search for the correct spelling finds nothing.
traps.fix:
-- up to 2020-21 the column is `panchyat`; from 2021-22 it is `lgd_vill_panchayat_name`
coalesce(lgd_vill_panchayat_name, panchyat) as panchayat

traps.what: Management code 7 reads 'Minority Affairs Dept.' in DCF 2021-22. It reads 'Partially Govt. Aided' in DCF 2025-26. Minority Affairs moves to code 89.
traps.cost: One fixed lookup across all years puts a government school in the aided sector.
traps.check: Read the DCF for the year in question, not the latest.
traps.fix:
-- code 7 is NOT the same thing before and after 2022-23
case when year <= '2021-22' and managment = '7' then 'Minority Affairs (State Govt)'
     when year >= '2022-23' and managment = '7' then 'Partially Govt Aided'
end

traps.what: DCF 2021-22 item 1.15(a) prints code 8 as Unrecognized and code 98 as Madarsa Unrecognized. The 2025-26 form drops both from its printed list. 21,330 schools still report them.
traps.cost: A lookup without them renders 21,330 schools and about 2.1 million children as NULL. We read that NULL as 'the State does not classify these schools'. The State does.
traps.check: Every code present in the data needs a row in the lookup, even one the current form no longer prints.
traps.fix:
-- 8 = Unrecognized, 98 = Madarsa Unrecognized (DCF 2021-22 item 1.15(a), type OT)
-- Both are dropped from the 2025-26 printed list and 21,330 schools still report them.
-- The Ministry counts them the same way: D.O. 23-2/2024-Stats gives 22,298 for 2023-24.
case when managment in ('8','98') then 'other' end

traps.what: A union of eight yearly files keeps every column any year ever had. These four ended at 2021-22. UDISE dropped them at the SDMIS break. The columns remain and read NULL for every later row.
traps.cost: `CASE WHEN x = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0` counts NULL as a No. Query drinking_water_available for 2025-26 and every state returns 0.0%. That reads as 'no school in India has drinking water'. UDISE stopped collecting the column four years earlier.
traps.check: Check the field's year span BEFORE querying it, not the value it returns. `select years from udise_field_span where field = ?` is the first query, not the last.
traps.fix:
-- ALWAYS check the span before the value
select field, years from udise_field_span where field = 'drinking_water_available';
-- ['2018-19','2019-20','2020-21','2021-22']  -> it ENDED at the SDMIS break.
-- Querying it for 2025-26 returns 0.0% in every state, which is not a finding.

traps.what: DCF 2.11(b) asks about a librarian. No gate sits above it. A school can therefore report a librarian and no library. 5,845 schools do. 4,633 of them report no library, no book bank and no reading corner. A further 9,596 report an ICT lab with zero computers.
traps.cost: Any librarian statistic must state which of the two fields it trusts.
traps.check: Test the constraint directly. Note that a ZERO violation rate elsewhere proves the form gates the question, not that the facility exists.
traps.fix:
-- count the contradiction before trusting either field
select count(*) from school_library
where year = '2025-26' and librarian_yn = 1 and library_availability = 2;
-- 5,845 schools, 3.3% of all librarian claims. In Bihar it is 19.1%.

traps.what: DCF 2.11(a) is one question with three rows. Karnataka government schools report 89.6% book bank. Rajasthan reports 17.6%.
traps.cost: A 72-point gap is not credible as provision. Do not compare these two fields across states.
traps.check: Compare a state's three rows against each other before comparing states.
traps.fix:
-- compare a state against ITSELF across the three rows, never across states
select state,
  avg(case when library_availability=1 then 100.0 else 0 end) as library,
  avg(case when book_bank=1 then 100.0 else 0 end)            as book_bank,
  avg(case when reading_corner=1 then 100.0 else 0 end)       as reading_corner
from school_library join school_year using (school_id, year)
where year='2025-26' group by 1;
-- Karnataka govt: 98.5 / 89.6 / 87.7.  Rajasthan govt: 77.8 / 17.6 / 27.9.
